clue.text: Romance taking place in Devon

definitions.meaning: a romance in the old sense is an adventure novel, here Charles Kingsley's 1855 seafaring tale of that title
a seaside village on the north Devon coast, named after the novel; Devon is a county in south-west England

explanation.surface: A love affair conducted somewhere in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romance' looks like a love affair, but it means a novel; the book and the Devon village share the name, the village having taken it from the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are proper names: Kingsley's adventure novel and the Devon resort village called after it.

clue.text: Trail left by party

definitions.meaning: the track of disturbed water left behind a boat
a gathering, especially an Irish one, held round the dead before a funeral

explanation.surface: A trail of litter left by revellers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the wash behind a moving vessel and a vigil-cum-gathering held for the dead.

clue.text: Barrage of indignation after pounds kept by bank

indicators.note: the anger comes after the rest
the bank holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a shelf is a sandbank or ledge under water
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra
ire is anger

explanation.surface: An outburst of fury after a bank holds on to customers' money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept by' and 'after' are the placing words. 'bank' wants to be a lender holding pounds; here it is a ledge or sandbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a heavy, sustained bombardment by artillery, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Disclose how age affected hopeless' search

indicators.note: letters affected are acted upon and changed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A command to reveal how ageing has altered someone on a futile quest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges DISCLOSEHOWAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a futile pursuit of something unattainable, a search with no hope of success.

clue.text: Put through routine to get badge

indicators.note: one piece runs through the middle of the other

parts.note: rote is mechanical routine, as in learning by rote
to set is to put or place

explanation.surface: Someone is drilled in a routine to earn a badge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put through' reads as drilling someone in a routine, but 'Put' is a piece of its own and 'through' places it inside the routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge, as awarded at shows or worn by party supporters.

clue.text: One no longer popular — was perfect

definitions.meaning: a person whose fame or success has faded
the verb 'was' put into the perfect tense

explanation.surface: Someone now out of favour was once flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfect' is the grammatical tense, not 'flawless': the perfect form of 'was' is the two-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a person past their prime; the two words are also the present perfect of 'be'.

clue.text: Retired, in charge of fixed points

indicators.note: something retired has gone back, so the pieces that follow are read backwards as a whole

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who has retired was once in charge of certain fixed locations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns the whole run IC + OF backwards, giving FO + CI.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry and optics these are fixed points, such as the two points defining an ellipse; the word is a plural.

clue.text: A month, and small number's left group

parts.note: OCT is the abbreviation for October

indicators.note: the number has left, taken out of the word and

parts.note: taken as written before its change
N is an abbreviation for number, small because it is cut down

explanation.surface: After a month, only a small number of a group remain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like 'remaining' but means departed: N goes from AND, leaving AD.
explanation.definitionFit: An octad is a group or set of eight things.

clue.text: Popular lady is taken round hill by legatees

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
her is the pronoun for a lady

indicators.note: the word is is wrapped round the hill

parts.note: taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A well-liked woman is guided round a hill by the people inheriting her estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken round' makes the word 'is' wrap the hill; a tor is a craggy hilltop typical of Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Legatees receive bequests under a will, so they are those who inherit.

clue.text: A bum summer once upset tissue lining nostril, for instance

indicators.note: upset letters are knocked over and end up in a new order

explanation.surface: A loafer was once ill over the summer with a nosebleed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges ABUMSUMMERONCE; 'bum' is a layabout, not a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: The moist lining of the nose is an example of this tissue, which lines body cavities and secretes mucus.

clue.text: Ring given by king to his lady friend

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
Nell Gwyn was the famous mistress of King Charles II

explanation.surface: A ring presented by a monarch to his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests jewellery but is the sound of a bell; Nell Gwyn, an actress, was Charles II's mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: A tolling bell, especially one rung for a death, is a ring of that solemn kind.

clue.text: Mythical creature — see it crouch down next to church

parts.note: 'it' is slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
to squat is to crouch down on one's heels

explanation.surface: Readers are told to look at a fabled beast hunkering beside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is only a pointer, as in 'see page 5'; 'it' is the old crossword term for sex appeal (SA).
explanation.definitionFit: The North American Bigfoot is a legendary ape-like creature of the forests, which makes it a beast of myth.

clue.text: Instrument on stairs in black box

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: a flight is a run of stairs
a recorder is a woodwind instrument

explanation.surface: A musical instrument left on a staircase inside a dark box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the instrument after the stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The black box is the everyday name for an aircraft's crash-proof data-logging device.

clue.text: Woman's frock being shortened could develop into a problem

indicators.note: the letters develop into something new, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the word with its S kept as a letter

indicators.note: a shortened word loses its tail, here its last letter

explanation.surface: A woman's dress, if taken up, might become a source of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being shortened' drops the K of FROCK; 'could develop into' rearranges WOMANSFROC.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is an apt image for a complicated problem that, once opened, releases more trouble.

clue.text: Fatty, a girl has put on a front

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, from Diana
to pose is to put on an affected manner

explanation.surface: A remark addressed to an overweight person, about a girl who is being pretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fatty' reads as a rude form of address but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose tissue is the body's fat store, so the word is an adjective meaning consisting of fat.

clue.text: It won't be a problem, not as we worked out

indicators.note: letters worked out are solved into a new arrangement, like a puzzle reshuffled

explanation.surface: A reassurance that something will be easy, though we have not yet solved it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' rearranges NOTASWE.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase is an idiom of reassurance: the task is easy and causes no trouble.

clue.text: Being former reserve, keeping gun

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the reserve holds the gun inside it

parts.note: ice means cold reserve of manner
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: Someone who used to be in the reserves still keeps a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' is the container signal. 'reserve' wants to mean reservist soldiers, but it is coldness of manner; 'former' is the usual crossword ex.
explanation.definitionFit: Being as a noun means the state of living or existing, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Waffles enough about providing accommodation for individual

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the run found is read backwards
the two words house the run of letters needed, giving it room inside them

explanation.surface: Someone talks evasively for long enough about housing a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'providing accommodation for' marks FLESENO inside wafFLES ENOugh; 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun stands for any single person considered by itself, an individual in the abstract.

clue.text: Lift crane's jib up, carrying first small quantity

indicators.note: the turned word carries the other piece inside it
in a down answer, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: to luff is to raise or lower a crane's jib
1ST, with the figure 1 read as I

explanation.surface: An operator raises a crane's arm, lifting the first small load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the crane word, giving FFUL, and 'carrying' holds 1st inside it; luffing is a crane operator's term for moving the jib up or down.
explanation.definitionFit: As much as a hand can hold, so a modest amount, as in a handful of coins.

clue.text: Shabbier soothsayer about to croak

indicators.note: the soothsayer is put around the other piece

parts.note: a seer foretells the future
croak is slang for die

explanation.surface: A fortune teller looking more dishevelled because he is about to die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of' with 'to croak', but it is the container signal, and 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy means shabby and run-down, so the comparative is a synonym.

clue.text: In other words, a rogue — but not very immoral

parts.note: SC is short for Latin scilicet, meaning namely or that is to say

indicators.note: the very is excluded, taken out of the rogue

parts.note: a varlet is an old word for a rascal

explanation.surface: Put differently, someone is a scoundrel, though not an especially wicked one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not very' drops the V from VARLET, leaving ARLET.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet describes sinfulness, as in a scarlet woman, so it can mean immoral.

clue.text: After game Jack goes to club with outside gathering at midnight

indicators.note: the word with is placed outside the rest

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the sailor comes after the game in the run

parts.note: chess is a board game
jack is a sailor, abbreviated AB (able seaman)
a bat is a club used in sport

explanation.surface: Following a game, Jack heads to a nightclub, with a crowd gathered outside at midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the word 'with' round the middle run; 'After' says the sailor follows the game. Jack is the sailor, as Jack Tar.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore held that witches met at midnight for a sabbath, a gathering of covens.

clue.text: Regularly trod piazza's stone

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Someone often walked over the stone of an Italian square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes letters 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 of 'trod piazza'.
explanation.definitionFit: Topaz is a gemstone, usually yellow, so it is an example of a stone.

clue.text: Design for garden

definitions.meaning: a scheme or plan, often a secret one
a small piece of ground for growing things

explanation.surface: A layout plan for a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a scheme and a small patch of land such as a vegetable bed.

clue.text: Laid-back four sleep restlessly

indicators.note: restless sleep tosses about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A relaxed group of four who nevertheless sleep badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restlessly' rearranges FOURSLEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something full of repose is calm and relaxed, which is a fair synonym for laid-back.

clue.text: Record first part of Tolstoy book at length

parts.note: Tolstoy's novel Anna Karenina begins with the name Anna

explanation.surface: A note about having read the opening of a Tolstoy novel at great length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first part' is not the first letter but the first word of the title Anna Karenina; 'at length' is not 'in detail' but L.
explanation.definitionFit: An annal is a record of a single year's events, singular of the usual plural for historical records.

clue.text: Measure of gelatinous mixture

definitions.meaning: a measurement or dimension, how big something is
a glue-like substance used to stiffen paper or prime plaster

explanation.surface: Measuring out a portion of jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: One word has both senses: the dimensions of something, and a gluey sealant used by decorators.

clue.text: Pick of the bunch needing good luck!

definitions.meaning: the finest ones of a group

explanation.surface: Choosing the finest of a bunch takes good fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the very finest items, and it is also a parting wish for success.
